after: ## The impact of the war: economic problems
alt: After the German invasion of June 1941 captured Ukraine and besieged Leningrad, the USSR responded by moving over 1,500 factories east, mobilising the whole economy, rationing food strictly and receiving Lend-Lease aid from the USA and Britain.
caption: Moving industry east and total mobilisation kept the war effort going.

alt: Around 27 million Soviet citizens died. Four further effects: civilian deaths in the siege of Leningrad, killings and deportations under occupation, millions of homes destroyed and children orphaned, and the deportation of whole nationalities in 1941 and 1944.
caption: No country lost more people in the war than the USSR.

alt: Balance of Stalin's war leadership: weaknesses (ignored warnings, purged officers, encirclements in 1941) against strengths (State Defence Committee, staying in Moscow, patriotic appeals, reliance on Zhukov). Below, the harsh Order No. 227 and a changed propaganda tone.
caption: Stalin's leadership was neither wholly good nor wholly bad.

after: ## Women in the Great Patriotic War
alt: Three stages for women: replacing men on the home front, serving in the armed forces (over 800,000 by common estimates, including the Night Witches), and demobilisation after the war. Below, women in propaganda: The Motherland Calls! poster and the tour of the sniper Lyudmila Pavlichenko.
caption: Women were vital to the war effort and to its propaganda, but little recognised afterwards.

alt: Three columns on reconstruction to 1953: industry was rebuilt under the Fourth Five-Year Plan and the atomic bomb tested in 1949; agriculture stagnated, with famine in 1946-47; and living standards were little better than in 1940.
caption: Heavy industry recovered; farming and living standards did not.

alt: Timeline of High Stalinism: Zhdanov's attacks on culture from 1946, the anti-cosmopolitan campaign from 1948, the Leningrad Affair, Stalin's seventieth birthday in 1949, the Gulag peak, the Doctors' Plot in January 1953, Stalin's death on 5 March 1953 and Beria's arrest and execution.
caption: Terror and the cult grew again after 1945, until Stalin's death in March 1953.

alt: Four steps of a model 6-mark answer: name one way (fewer workers in the villages), support it with detail, explain its effect on people, and show the change lasted beyond 1945.
caption: One way, developed with detail, effect and lasting consequence.
